question: What circle did Antoine Arnauld find in the road Descartes took to certainty?
answer: God propped up by clear ideas, and clear ideas by God. Descartes trusted clear and distinct perception because a good God would not deceive him, yet proved God from clearly perceived premises, as Arnauld objected in 1641. Descartes replied that an insight held in view needs no guarantee; only the memory of one does.
move: Check whether the proof of a guarantee already relies on the guarantee.
reference: Descartes, Fourth Set of Objections and Replies, in The Philosophical Writings of Descartes II, trans. Cottingham, Stoothoff & Murdoch, Cambridge University Press, 1984
